body:
Secret Squirrel wrote:
> 
> On Tue, 13 May 1997, Shadow wrote:
> 
> 
> You don't have to have a car.  It depends a lot on other things in your
> life.
> 
> You can get a rack for a bicycle and a couple of baskets hung on the
> rack, and carry loads up to 50-100 pounds.  One can do shopping that way.
> 
> A bicycle can be complementary to a car -- you don't have to think of it
> as either get rid of the car or don't.  Bicycles are good for short
> trips, which are hard on cars' engines.  You'll have much fewer car
> expenses if you use the car only for the occasional long trip, or for
> carrying really large loads.
> 
> 
> I think that driving is violent.  Cars are weapons, like hammers from
> hell smashing anyone in their way out of this world.  Bicycling is
> better because it's at peace with the world.  It's soothing to bicycle,
> it puts one in touch with the world and it's good for your body.
> One is unlikely to seriously hurt anyone on a bicycle.
> 
> I suggest that people ask themselves before getting in the car
> whether they really need to drive, or whether they can take a
> bicycle instead or get what they're looking for in some other way.
> 
> I like to think when I'm going along on my bicycle smiling, shopping on my
> bicycle, that I'm giving people seditious thoughts like "do I really
> need to be in this great metal cage?"
> 
>                                 Nick Halloway

Very well spoken. Except that some of us find ourselves stuck in the
sort of community where it's very difficult to ride your bike anywyere
without risking being sideswiped by maniacal cars. Or having water
splashed on you, or having the drivers shout things at you... unless you
live in a nice civilized town with quiet streets, you are taking your
life in your hands by riding a bike or walking. Plus, it's not very
pleasant. And in many cases, when the nearest store is several miles
away and you are shopping for a family, it is nearly impossible to get
the job done by riding a bike.

Once our car broke down & we had no transportation for a week. I learned
how much physical energy the "primitive" folks expend, just getting from
place to place. Only, today it is worse for the carless.. because
automobiles have totally altered the environment to the benefit of the
drivers & the detriment of everyone else. 

I have heard that in the 30's or so, the auto manufacturers made a
secret agreement with the government to encourage the building of roads
at the detriment of railroads. Had this not happened, perhaps our cities
would never have evolved into the auto-dependent suburban sprawl they
have become.

". In many cases the new technology changes society so that eventually
people find themselves forced to use it. For example, consider motorized
transport. ...the introduction of motorized transport soon changed
society .. so as to restrict greatly man's freedom of locomotion. ..the
arrangement of our cities has changed in such a way that the majority or
people no longer live within walking distance of their place of
employment...so that they have to depend on the autombile for
transportation. When a new item of tech. is introduced as an option ....
it does not necesarily remain optional"

paraphrased from
The Unabomber Manifesto, para. 127
